title: Handles break the neat circle
hook: Which estimate avoids the pictured handle overlap?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that each handle adds to the width a mug needs, so fewer mugs fit in a row than the diameter alone suggests

misconception: To count how many mugs fit in a row, divide the width by the mug's diameter.
objective: Counting only cup diameters ignores their handles. The conservative side-by-side layout uses the complete horizontal envelope for each empty cup.

claims.text: Each cup needs its full envelope along the row, 9 + 3 = 12 cm: 48 ÷ 12 = 4. Counting only the 9 cm body gives 5, and they collide at the handles. Other layouts may interleave handles.
claims.source: Recall transfer item for this lesson; scenario values are stipulated in the question. The why applies the lesson's own model and limits (see this lesson's idea, limit and formula claims). Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. FC LH-3B (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): DISPUTED. Arithmetic is right (48/12=4; 48/9=5), but the question does not say which way the handles point. With the handles turned toward the tray depth instead of along the row, 5 cups (45 cm) fit side by side without handles overlapping, so option "5" is also correct on a literal reading, and the why's "they collide at the handles" holds only for handles along the row (as drawn in HomeLesson.tsx handle-envelope). Fix (example wording, owner decides): question "Cups are 9 cm across, with a 3 cm handle pointing along the row. With handles not allowed to overlap, how many fit across a 48 cm tray?" See company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH3-2026-10-14.md (Batch B). Revised by demo-builder 2026-10-14 (W-388): question now states the fix (see recall-patch-home.lines.txt); status reset to unverified for fact-check re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Read the handle-envelope scene first; the stage draws the handles along the row. The recall question now states 'a 3 cm handle pointing along the row'. Arithmetic: 9 + 3 = 12 and floor(48/12) = 4; body only, floor(48/9) = 5, which would need 4 handle gaps of 3 cm (57 cm > 48). Even with handles interleaved two to a gap, 5 cups need 45 + 3 × 3 = 54 cm > 48, so 4 is the maximum for any side-by-side layout and the keyed answer is uniquely right. The why's 'Other layouts may interleave handles' is a hedge, not an extra answer. Checked as a fresh instance under W-280 (the wording follows an earlier fact-checker example), after reading the artifact.

recall.question: Cups are 9 cm across, with a 3 cm handle pointing along the row. Side by side, with handles not allowed to overlap, how many fit across a 48 cm tray?
recall.why: Each cup needs its full envelope along the row, 9 + 3 = 12 cm: 48 ÷ 12 = 4. Counting only the 9 cm body gives 5, and they collide at the handles. Other layouts may interleave handles.
